sentences.sentence: Move more: at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous aerobic physical activity; muscle-strengthening activities at least twice per week; several hours of light physical activity including standing [1].
Sleep well: 7 to 9 hours of good-quality sleep on a regular basis, with consistent bed and wake times [1].

passages.text:
[Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Adults aged 18-64 > 24-Hour Movement Guidelines (adults 18-64) - summary]
- Move more: at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous aerobic physical activity; muscle-strengthening activities at least twice per week; several hours of light physical activity including standing. - Reduce sedentary time: 8 hours or less of sedentary time per day, including no more than 3 hours of recreational screen time, and break up long periods of sitting. - Sleep well: 7 to 9 hours of good-quality sleep on a regular basis, with consistent bed and wake times. - Some activity is better than none; progress gradually.

[Accuracy of PHQ-2/PHQ-9 and GAD-2/GAD-7 screening questionnaires > Screening questionnaires used by MapleMind > Anxiety: GAD-2 then GAD-7]
- Recommended cut-points are 3 or more on the GAD-2 and 10 or more on the GAD-7 (Kroenke et al. 2010). A meta-analysis found GAD-7 sensitivity 0.83 and specificity 0.84 at a cut-off of 8 for generalized anxiety disorder, with cut-offs 7-10 performing similarly. - GAD-7 severity bands: 0-4 minimal, 5-9 mild, 10-14 moderate, 15-21 severe.

[OurCare National Survey 2025 - access to primary care in Canada > Primary care access (OurCare 2025) > Implication]
Many Canadians who screen positive for depression or anxiety, or who want help with weight-related health, have no regular clinician to follow up with. Navigation must therefore include options that do not require a family doctor (for example 811 health lines, walk-in clinics, community mental health agencies and crisis lines).

**Where to get support**
- Most provinces: dial 8-1-1 to talk to a registered nurse (tell me your province for the exact service).
- Community counselling: find your local Canadian Mental Health Association branch - https://cmha.ca/find-your-cmha/
- No family doctor? Walk-in clinics, pharmacists and 8-1-1 can help you start; ask about publicly funded counselling.
